content: The provided text is a detailed dataset and commentary on blood transfusion and plasma fractionation practices across various countries from 2011 to 2013. 1. The data on the number of blood component units issued or transfused in Montenegro only includes information from the blood transfusion center in the country. 2. The figures provided represent the units of blood components issued, not necessarily transfused. 3. Partial data is available for some countries, and in certain cases, only subnational data is reported. 4. In Lagos State, Nigeria, the data reflects the activities of the Lagos State Blood Transfusion Service, and no national-level data is available. 5. In Papua New Guinea, the data on blood components issued or transfused only covers the Blood Transfusion Service in Port Moresby. 6. In Peru, the data for 2011–2013 includes the number of hospitals performing blood transfusions and the units of blood components issued or transfused, excluding autologous blood units. 7. In the Philippines, the reported data includes both whole blood-derived platelets and apheresis platelets, but not all facilities provided complete data on transfusions. 8. In Poland, the data includes subnational figures, and cryosupernatant is included in the plasma data. 9. In Portugal, the National Institute of Transfusion Medicine provides data only for issued blood units, and cryosupernatant is included in the plasma data. 10. In Qatar, the data for 2013 includes units of blood components issued or transfused, but earlier years lack comprehensive reporting. 11. In the Republic of Korea, the Korean Red Cross produced half-finished plasma products supplied to commercial sectors, and the country imported significant volumes of plasma in 2012. 12. In Rwanda, the data for 2011–2013 includes partial figures, with some years lacking complete information on transfused units. 13. In Saint Kitts and Nevis, the data for 2013 includes the number of blood component units issued or transfused, but earlier years lack comprehensive reporting. 14. In Senegal, the data for 2011–2013 includes units of blood components issued or transfused, with partial data for some years. 15. In Serbia, the data includes the number of hospitals performing blood transfusions and the units of blood components issued or transfused, with partial data for some years. 16. In Thailand, the data for 2011–2013 includes the number of hospitals performing blood transfusions and the units of blood components issued or transfused, with subnational data provided by the National Blood Centre in Bangkok. 23. In Timor-Leste, only the National Hospital and Clinic in Dili distributes blood to patients, and the data for 2011–2013 reflects this limited scope. 24.
